label: paragraph_title
text: REACHED CANTON.

label: text
text: DANISH WORLD FLIGHT PROGRESS.

label: text
text: UNEXPECTED ARRIVAL

label: text
text: Following Captinin D'Oisy's

label: text
text: (An Occasional Correspondent.)

label: text
text: Rather unexpectedly although they were two days late, the Danish world flier, arrived here this afternoon.

label: text
text: At first the airman was due on Saturday. Inclement weather, boisterous wind, poor visibility, heavy rain and generally unfavourable flying conditions led local people to think that the departure from Hanoi would not be made for some days.

label: text
text: About 1 p.m. to-day, the aeroplane was over the city. After looking about, the airman found the landing place at Tai-sha-tau and came down safely. Only a few guards and a mechanic or two were on duty. They helped the visitor to put away his machine in the shed, and a telephone message was sent through to the Aviation Bureau. The Chief and about twenty others immediately rushed down to Tai-sha-tau, (off the East Bund) to welcome the flies:

label: text
text:
After the usual felicitations, it was decided to accord the official welcome on April 13 (yesterday).
I am told that the aviator effected a good landing. He left Hanoi at 8 p.m. and flew the 550 miles in five hours. It is not known when he will put off for Shanghai.

label: paragraph_title
text: OTHER FLIGHTS

label: text
text: Captain D'Oisy, the French aviator, also took five hours to do the Hanoi-Canton stage. His machine was of 400 horse-power and his speed of 110 miles (for that leg) was described as extraordinary. D'Oisy also landed at Tai-sha-tau, shortly after the premature report of the death of Dr. Sun Yat-sen.

label: text
text: Major Zanni, the Argentine tier who was nearly drowned as the result of a collision (while in a small boat) in Hongkong, failed to arrive in Canton as his aeroplane was damaged while putting off from Hanoi. He then used his seaplane, "came on" to "Hongkong and proceeded North where earlier the delay prevented him from completing his flight.

label: text
text: Details of the Venture.

label: text
text: Two land machines, built in Denmark and equipped with Lorraine-Dietrich 400 h.p. motors of the newest model started from Copenhagen on March 16. The following route was followed: — Lemberg, Constantinople, Aleppo (March 22), Bagdad, Buschir, Bender Abbas, Karachi, Agra, Calcutta (March 31) and Rangoon (April 3).

label: text
text: At Rangoon, Lieut. Herschend was forced to land 28 miles away, on account of engine trouble. Lieut. Botved has since continued the flight to Bangkok and Hanoi, and his arrival at Canton is now reported.

label: text
text: The next stop is Shanghai, 800 miles away. D'Oisy went from Canton to Shanghai in 9½ hours.

label: text
text: miles away. D'Oisy went from Canton to Shanghai in 9½ hours. The rest of the projected trip is by way of Peking, Taiku, and Tokyo, and return by the same route.

label: text
text:
Each of the two Danish Flying Corps officers is accompanied by a non-commissioned officer.
The machines are marked "Denmark R1" and "Denmark R2," with the red and white colours. Two extra motors were forwarded to Tokyo—one to Bangkok and one to Karachi.

label: paragraph_title
text: DR. HO'S OFFER.

label: text
text: WILLING TO FIGHT ANOTHER ELECTION.

label: text
text: AN APPEAL LODGED.

label: text
text: Dr. S. C. Ho has sent to us, with a request for publication, a copy of the following letter in regard to the Sanitary Board election:—

label: text
text:
Hongkong, April 18, 1926.
Dr. F. M. G. Ozorio, Hongkong.

label: text
text: Dear Dr. Ozorio,—As I feel that yesterday's election was unsatisfactory both to you and myself as the candidates, and to the electors who evinced such public spirit in the matter as to turn out in such large numbers, but only to be literally "shut out," I write to inform you that, if you are desirous of standing again and of having another election forthwith, I shall be very happy to do whatever I can to achieve this object.

label: text
text: I notice in to-day's issue of the "South China Morning Post" that you are reported to have said:—

label: text
text: “I think the election was very unfair. The electors didn't have a chance to vote. I know I had at least 700 to 800 votes, and most of them were not recorded.”

label: text
text: I sympathise with you that so many of your supporters were not given a chance to vote, but I feel that I can claim your sympathy when I tell you—in fairness to my own supporters—that very many of them found the Registry an impregnable fortress and were unable even to obtain admittance.

label: text
text: You may recall that, at the time, I myself suggested that in view of the circumstances—and I feel that the authorities were not to blame, because they could hardly be prepared for the unprecedented interest taken by the public—the election should be adjourned to another date so as to give all a chance to vote. I recollect that I could not enlist your support in this regard: indeed, I gathered that your view was that the election had better go on.

label: text
text: Holding the same views before as well as after the election, I am only too anxious that the electors should be given every opportunity of returning to office the candidate of their real choice, and I have no wish to act as a member of the Sanitary Board's unless I feel that I have the confidence of the majority of the electors.

label: text
text: Will you kindly inform me as soon as possible of your views in this matter.

label: text
text: As the question of election is a matter of great public interest I am sending a copy of this letter to the Press.—Yours faithfully, S. C. Ho:

label: paragraph_title
text: Dr. Ozorlo's Reply

label: text
text: Dr. F. M. Graca Ozorio sends us for publication the following copy of his reply to Dr. Ho's letter:—

label: text
text:
Hongkong, April 14, 1926.
Dr. S. O. Ho,

label: text
text: Hongkong

label: text
text: Dear Dr. Ho, — I have to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of yesterday with thanks. After perusing the contents therein I am very pleased to note the spirit of self-sacrifice, which is such a dominant trait in the medical profession, is so well reflected in you.

label: text
text: As you are well aware, the reason for my accepting my nomination was the sense of civic duty, which also undoubtedly actuated your acceptance. The large number of electors who went to the poll on Monday last, believed the saying that civic spirit in Hongkong is dormant.

label: text
text: As the last election, as you yourself expressed, was unsatisfactory to all concerned, and in justice to the electors, I have had no recourse but to lodge a protest with His Excellency the Governor in Council against the validity of the said election, a copy of which I am enclosing for your information.

label: text
text:
As the matter is sub-judice. I regret I cannot accept or refuse your very kind and sporting offer though I am grateful to you for it and must await and abide by the decision of His Excellency the Governor in Council.
I am sending a copy of this letter to the Press, not only because the election is a matter of public interest, but to take the opportunity of tendering my thanks to you publicly.
(Sg.) F. M. GRADA OZONIO
(Continued on Page 9.)

label: doc_title
text: CANTON HEALTH.

label: text
text: WHAT PUBLIC BUREAU DOES IN A MONTH

label: text
text: LEPROSY AND SMALL-POX.

label: text
text: Some very interesting information is given in the monthly report of the Canton Bureau of Public Health.

label: text
text: Dr. Sze-to, the Commissioner, is a highly-respected official. He refers to work for lepers and a campaign against small-p)x. His report includes:—

label: text
text: Three cases of air-bleven and water-injected pork for sale were reported against butchers.

label: text
text:
At the request of the Bureau of Public Safety for the Accination of the police, instructions were given to the various public health organizations and hospitals to vaccinate all members of the police force.
18 lepers were detected and sent to the new Lenny Hospital outside of the L. J. L. and while to inspect and released after due examination

label: text
text: und released after due exaustion.

label: text
text: On March 25, 15 lepers, male and female, were handed over to the Leprosy Hospital at Shoklung. The water of the Water-work on two occasions was reported to be below the standard of purity.

label: text
text: 11 coffins were temporarily sheltered in the public mortuaries: 12 removed therefrom and 11 transported to and from out-districts.

label: text
text: Licences given for sale of two kinds of special drugs after analysis.

label: text
text: Lau Ah-sam, a Canton citizen, who had kept his dead father's coffin (bier,) within his residence for a long period, was ordered to remove it for interment within 3 days.

label: paragraph_title
text: Small-pox Campaign

label: text
text: In order to guard against small-pox, special attention was devoted to a campaign for vaccination.

label: text
text: In the crowded parts of the city, 54 centres were selected for carrying out a vaccination campaign. On March 3, a joint conference was convened at the Municipal Hospital, at which the staff and students of the Hackett Medical School, the Kwong Wah Medical College, the Sino-Franco Medical College, the Medical Division of the National University, the Tau-keung, the Women and Children's Hospital, etc. attended. The vaccinators started work in the various sections from March 4 to March 11 for one week, with the result that 31,018 persons were vaccinated.

label: text
text: This campaign aroused widespread public interest and showed that the citizens of Canton readily appreciated the value of this prophylactic measure. The report closes by stating that the training of the Sanitary Police will be continued.

text: The Coast Inspector for Shanghai has issued a notice that on or about May 4, 1926, the "Tungsha" light-vessel, moored in the South Channel entrance to the Yangtze River, will be withdrawn from her station and replaced by the new light-vessel "Tungsha". The new light-vessel has a red hull with "Tungsha" on her side, a foremast with spherical daymark, an iron column surmounted by a lantern and a mainmast with spherical daymark. label: paragraph_title
text: OBITUARY.

label: text
text: LATE MR. A. W. J. HOY:

label: text
text: We regret to record the death of Mr. A. W. J. Hoy, engineer, of Holt's Wharf, which occurred at the Kowloon Hospital at 2 a.m. today.

label: text
text: Mr. Hoy, who was 39 years of age, had been connected with Holt's Wharf for eight years and was very well known in Kowloon and Hongkong. Prior to settling down here he had been an engineer on Blue Funnel ships engaged in the China trade and for a period he held a responsible position in connection with harbour supervision in Singapore.

label: text
text: As a non-playing member of the Kowloon Football Club he took a keen interest in the welfare of the team and he was also a playing member of the Kowloon Bowling Green Club.

label: text
text: The late Mr. Hoy will be missed by the Institute of Engineers and Shipbuilders, of which he was a Committee member.

label: text
text: News of his death came as a great shock there as elsewhere for Mr. Hoy was of good physique and prior to going to Hospital had complained merely of a severe cold.

label: text
text: Death is attributed to pneumonia following an attack of pleurisy. Mr. Hay had been in Hospital since Friday.

label: text
text: The late Mr. Hoy was also well known in connection with local Masonic activities, holding the position of Master of Zetland Lodge and being a member of the District Grand Lodge of Hongkong and S. China. He was third principal of the Victoria Chapter and a member of other Masonic institutions in the Colony.

label: text
text: The late Mr. Hoy had lived for some time at Windsor, Lodge, Kowloon. He leaves a wife and child who left for home two months ago and with whom generus sympathy will be felt in their suden bereavements.

label: text
text: The funeral passes the monument at 5 p.m. to-day.

label: paragraph_title
text: CUPID'S DART.

label: paragraph_title
text: MATCH-MAKER WHO WAS NOT SATISFIED.

label: text
text: A COURT SEQUEL

label: text
text:
The protracted stay of a matchmaker at the house of a Dairy Farm employee whom he had united to a woman from Macao led to trouble and he had to appear at the Central Magistracy this morning on a charge of possession of a dagger and larceny.
Evidence was given that the defendant received $30 for arranging the match, but continued to stay in the house at Pokfulam. The husband of the woman eventually had to put him out. Returning one morning at 5 o'clock during the absence of the husband, he demanded money from the woman. On being refused, he threatened to kill the husband, and walking into the house he took some copper cents from a till. He was stated to have carried the knife in his hand at the time of his visit.

label: text
text: Defendant was convicted and sentenced to four months' hard

label: paragraph_title
text: CHINESE HUMOUR.

label: text
text: AN ARTICLE IN A LOCAL NEWSPAPER.

label: text
text: PUBLISHER SUMMONED

label: text
text: was summoned to appear before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning for publishing matter in the Chinese language without the permission of the Secretary for Chinese Affairs. Sub Inspector Shukla said that the article which appeared in the issue of April 2 had not been submitted to the S.C.A. although a warning had been issued last month not to publish matter without submitting for censorship. He thought the present article was of an anti-foreign nature and bore a hidden meaning which was that the Chinese are willing to kow-tow to Europeans and not help their own people.

label: text
text: At the outset, Mr. E. S. C. Brooks defending, tendered a plea of guilty and asked for leniency by pointing out that the censorship was instituted during the commencement of the strike and that the regulations were not strictly carried out now, as they were no longer necessary. He termed the article in question as a mild satire in regard to a gentle man who gave $10,000 for a charitable cause and refused to allow time to a tenant to pay his rent of $30.

label: text
text:
The translation of the article stated that a fat, rich gentleman sitting in a rocking chair with spring, wind all over his face (meaning an affable countenance) was chatting with a long-nosed gentleman, the result being that the latter secured a cheque for $10,000 which was later ascertained to have gone to the authorities at "X port" for a building fund. The next day a thin man dressed in rags (a peasant) appeared before the gentleman in the rocking chair to ask for an extension of time to pay his rent of $30 owing to the failure of his crops, but the gentleman's countenance turning to one of anger, the peasant was refused hearing and driven by a servant.
An in-depth of the S.G.A department was questioned. Her His Worship as to the impression gained by a reader of the article. He said that the "long-nosed gentleman" was an allusion to a European and that "X port" stood for Hongkong. His Worship remarked that he gathered the Chinese were open-handed with foreigners but close-fisted in dealing with their own people.

label: text
text: The case concluded with a fine of $100.

label: paragraph_title
text: STRIKE PICKETS.

label: text
text: WARRANT FOR ARREST OF NO. 2 CHIEF.

label: text
text: ALLEGED DISAPPEARANCE.

label: text
text:
According to Canton vernacular papers, a warrant has been issued (not by the Government but by the Strike Executive) for the arrest of the deputy chief of the "Communications Department."
The "Communications Department" is in charge of pickets. Whilst the chief was away from Canton, on duty, the No. 2 is alleged to have acted for him, and then to have absent himself on the No. 1's return.

label: text
text: Canton papers also refer to the detention, in Chinese territory, just across the Macao border (in Chinshan) of the second principal Chinese police detective of Macao, by the boycott pickets. It is stated that a death penalty has been applied for on the grounds of alleged lack of sympathy when the anti-Canton risking (by so-called pro-Chan adherents) in the Heungshan district last year, caused some of the pickets to seek sanctuary in, or near Macao.

label: text
text: For being found asleep while in charge of the Praya East Police Station, a Chinese constable was fined $50 at the Magistracy this morning. During six months of the man's total service of one year, the record showed that he had ten reports all of a serious nature.
